transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery so far?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So you should be fine to get back to that fairly soon. Just avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous work for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice! I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! It's safe to continue using your eye gel for dry eyes unless you've been told otherwise by your care team. If you're running low, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful to know, thank you! I'm also experiencing a lot of sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Some sensitivity to bright light is normal as your eye adjusts to the new lens. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Some sensitivity to bright light is normal as your eye adjusts to the new lens. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Oh, alright. Also, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery. It should improve quickly and settle down over time. How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for explaining that. My surgery was just a few days ago, so I'll keep an eye on it. I don't have any more questions at the moment. Thanks for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's great! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and don't hesitate to contact your care team if you have any concerns.

verdict.label: fail
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` and `mild_case_advice` in the turn starting "Some sensitivity to bright light is normal...". However, the `escalation_criteria` point was not conveyed at any point in the conversation, as the agent was interrupted before it could deliver the full message about red-flag symptoms.
